scope: Illustrative incremental cooling design, not a disclosed Microsoft site or company valuation

assumptions.water_intensity: Illustrative avoided direct cooling-water intensity; the similar 0.30 figure in MS2 has consumption/withdrawal wording ambiguity and is not treated as a calibrated site input.
assumptions.electricity: Constant IT load; extra facility electricity equals IT MWh times incremental PUE. No renewable matching or carbon-credit value assumed.
assumptions.benefit: Recurring pre-tax incremental operating cash benefit. Zero initially; break-even is solved, not forecast. Avoided disruption and enabled profit must not be double counted.
assumptions.tax: 25% illustrative cash tax on water expense savings/benefits; costs/depreciation deductible by stated fractions. Delayed deduction cases shift shields by whole years, retaining charges, and include tax-only receipts beyond asset life. No deduction expiry or jurisdiction-specific law asserted.
assumptions.timing: All incremental capex at time zero; operating cash flow and tax depreciation start after commissioning; benefits occur at year-end for the full asset life.
assumptions.exclusions: Existing cooling route excludes terminal value, financing, holding costs, new IT hardware and working capital. Added-capacity route includes its own hardware replacements and working capital but assumes zero residual value, constant unit economics and no financing. Neither route quantifies supply-chain water or claims actual issuer economics.
assumptions.reliability: At most one water-linked event/year. Expected avoided loss = probability × duration × risk reduction × protected pre-tax cash contribution/hour × unrecoverable workload fraction. Protected contribution is after avoidable costs, not revenue. No Microsoft probability, loss or site forecast.
assumptions.capacity: Separate incremental new-capacity project with infrastructure/cooling and IT hardware capex, recurring total facility power and other costs, five-year hardware replacements, working capital and taxes. No terminal hardware value. New-capacity economics must not be counted again as an existing-workload benefit.

issuer_evidence_gaps: Matched site/design pair, withdrawal versus consumption definitions, water source and delivery contract
Cooling-specific incremental capex, realized PUE, maintenance, useful life and tax treatment
Water-linked disruption probability/duration before and after cooling change, including correlated power/heat events
Protected nonrecoverable cash contribution after rerouting/recovery and avoidable costs; contractual loss allocation
Water design demonstrably binding for new capacity, plus billable demand, prices and grid/power permits
All added-capacity infrastructure, hardware replacement, operating costs, working capital and taxes
